To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the 2010 early data from the LHC can be used to discover top-partners in composite Higgs models with mass of up to 500 GeV, and to measure their masses.

(a) the early LHC data can already probe the existence of top-partners with a mass of about 300 GeV in a realistic composite-Higgs model; (b) the discovery of a new exotic quark of charge 5 /3 would be a strong hint for a composite-Higgs scenario.

the 2010 early LHC collision run will allow to discover top-partners in the mass range from 150 GeV to 300 GeV, if their couplings to quarks and gluons are not too different from the Standard Model top-quark couplings.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the search for new physics in the early LHC data, in the framework of composite Higgs models.
the discovery potential of new physics at the LHC, and in particular of top-partner states in realistic composite Higgs models.
the discovery potential of new quarks in composite Higgs models.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the LHC has the discovery potential to observe the new quarks predicted in this model, and to reconstruct their masses, with the early LHE data.
a 5σ observation of same-sign dilepton or trilepton events with the LHC early data, with no evidence of jets in the final states, would be an unmistakable signature of a composite Higgs model.

, if the Higgs boson mass is in the range 130-200 GeV, and if a 5σ deviation is seen in the dilepton invariant mass distribution in the 2010 data, then this would provide strong evidence for a composite Higgs boson.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a realistic composite Higgss model, with a realistic spectrum of top-partners, can yield a 3-5σ excess over Standard Model expectation in early LHC collision events, which can be interpreted as evidence of the new physics.
the early LHC data will be able to discover a composite Higgs if the top-partner is light.

, with a few hundred pb−1 of data collected during 2011 at the LHC, it will be possible to discover new quarks with masses up to 600 GeV and to determine their masses with an accuracy of a few tens of GeV.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a realistic composite Higgss model can be tested with the early Lhc data, and that the top-partners of the model can be reconstructed with good precision.

, in a composite Higgs model, a light top-partner can be observed at the LHC with a relatively modest integrated luminosity, and that its mass and other properties can be measured in a relatively model-independent way.
the discovery of a new quark with charge 5/ 3 would provide strong evidence for a new strong dynamics sector at a TeV scale.
